answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to post a refundable bond, then slash it when that identity is caught double-claiming rewards or violating a challenge rule. Rewards accrue only after a bond has remained at risk through several rounds, so splitting one agent into an ivory island of aliases does not multiply free claims. A sybil attacker must lock up capital for each identity and risks losing it, making large-scale impersonation costly rather than merely a matter of generating names on a dune.
